rows.why: Most of S1 is plain adding-up, but the rows '2d' = 172800000 and '1d0h0m0s0ms' = 86400000 depend on whether a 'd' unit exists. Item 6 asks that and picks d = 86400000 ms, which matches. Item 9 (zero values) is related but covers fewer rows.
Item 1 asks whether whitespace around a duration is allowed. It picks trimming leading and trailing whitespace, so '  45m\n' parses to 2700000.

S3 mixes several questions. The biggest group of rows is '1.5h', '-3s', '+3s' and '３s', which is item 7's question (fractional, signed or non-digit counts). Item 7 rejects anything but ASCII digits, which matches. Items 2, 3 and 5 match the whitespace, uppercase and bare-number rows. Item 9, though, accepts leading zeros like '007s', which conflicts with the row '05s' being rejected.
No item asks whether a count may exceed the next unit up (e.g. '90m' instead of '1h30m'). Item 4 only covers unit order and repeats.
Item 4 asks about unit order and repeats. It requires strictly decreasing order and rejects repeats, so '30m1h', '1h1h', '1s500ms2s' and '5ms1s' all fail as S5 expects.
Item 8 asks about the upper limit. Its cap of 2^53-1 ms is exactly 9007199254740991, so the largest duration parses.

Item 8 asks what happens above the limit. It returns a 'duration ... exceeds' error with overflow-safe checks, so a total one over the cap and a huge ms count are both rejected with 'duration' in the message.

Item 12 asks how formatting picks units and skips zero components. Using d as the largest unit and omitting zeros gives '1d', '1m30s', '1h30m' and '1d1h1m1s1ms'. The row 0 → '0ms' is item 10's question, which also agrees.
With d as the largest unit and zero components skipped, 9007199254740991 formats as '104249991d8h59m991ms'. Seconds are 0, so they are left out.
No item asks whether formatting and then parsing gives the same number back.

Item 11 asks how formatting handles negative or too-large values. It returns an empty string and an error below 0 or above 2^53-1, which covers -1, 2^53, MinInt64 and MaxInt64. The pick doesn't say whether the message contains 'milliseconds'.
